drills.title: vs belyjudegwapo (730) — Kings Pawn Opening
drills.coachNote: White's pawn is one step from d4, and once it lands, Nxd4 plants a knight right in the center while his b2/e4 bishop pair still bears down on your kingside. Bd7 ignored all that and just developed quietly; after d4, exd4, Nxd4 your huge +4 edge got cut by three pawns for nothing. d5 fixes it at the source - it hits the bishop on e4 with tempo and takes the sting out of d4, and even the piece sac Bxh7+ Kxh7 Nxe5 Bxe5 Bxe5 still leaves you comfortably ahead. When a central break is brewing, answer it with a pawn move of your own instead of quietly developing.

drills.title: vs belyjudegwapo (730) — Kings Pawn Opening
drills.coachNote: White wants Rxa1, just scooping up your stray bishop since nothing is bothering his king and nothing blocks the rook getting there. Kxf8 grabbed the loose bishop on f8 first, but that let White play exactly that - Rxa1, Bf5, Nc5, f3 - and the piece came right back, shaving nearly two pawns off your +7 advantage. Bd4+ first changes the story: the check forces Kh1, and only then do you take Kxf8, keeping the bishop safe and the extra material locked in. When one of your pieces is hanging, check whether it can deliver check or create a threat on its way out before you let it go.

drills.coachNote: White wants e5, kicking anything on f6 and grabbing time it can spend on development, or worse if you handle it carelessly.
